Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game End 5 Cards in Each Deck Overview Play cards to manipulate your own and your opponents' displays, but be careful not to exceed 25 in card and token values. Turn First, draw a card, either from the deck, or the top card of the (face up) discard pile. Then either play a card or discard a card from your hand. If you play a card, it can either be played face up or face down. If you want to play a card face up, you have to be able to fully resolve it, otherwise it cannot be played this way. If you play a card face down, its effect is ignored and so is its value, but you can always check your face-down cards. If you discard a card from your hand instead of playing it, you can flip up a face-down card, activating its ability. If the total of your face-up cards (plus tokens on them) exceeds 25 at the end of your turn, you are eliminated. If you play an effect which causes another player to exceed 25 in faceup cards and tokens, you eliminate them and score 1VP. If you meet exactly 25, you end the round and score 1VP. Round End The round can end in a number of ways If a player has a value of 25 in their display, they gain 1VP If all but one player have been eliminated, the remaining player gains 1VP If the deck is depleted, the player with the highest value below 25 gains 1VP A new round commences with the player who most recently gained a VP Game End The game ends immediately when a player gains their 3rd VP, they win! [Rating: 1/10] It's sort of like Blackjack, except every single card has a unique ability. Therefore turns take 21x as long, gotta read all your cards and scan all the possible targets. In the end it's not even that interactive, nobody really cares what's happening on the table with others.

[Rating: 2/10] I think there's a very interesting and clever riff on blackjack here, but I need more exposure before I can reasonably assess exactly how much real agency the players have vs. how much of the game is merely luck of the draw. Further thoughts pending.

[Rating: 3/10] Rare BGA where we abandoned before finishing.  I don't think it's poorly made necessarily, but I didn't have any fun playing it, so I probably won't play it again.  I didn't really like having so many non-turns of me just playing a card face down in front of me, with seemingly rare opportunities to flip them face-up again (seems like maybe a card effect on a couple cards did, but you have to be lucky to draw them in the first place, which I rarely was). [Rating: 3/10] The special abilities on each card slowed the game down, this would improve with repeated plays but I didn't feel the need to play it again and again when there are better quick filler games out there

[Rating: 4/10] Not my sort of game anyway, but I played right after learning (and forgetting half of) Carnegie. I'd play again, but I wouldn't suggest it.

[Rating: 4/10] This can be fun if a bit silly filler. You have some control but other players can throw wrenches in your plan(s) - you hope to either force another player over 25 or be closest to 25 when the deck runs out. Each number has a different effect besides counting towards your 25.  Edit - after a four player game I reduced the rating to a 4 (from a 6). With 4 players the round is over so quickly and I felt I had very little agency in the game.
